set.body:
Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: Retain P3 deferred milestone. Frame extraction has already occurred (docs/module-relations.md); the historical incubated-Frame wording below is superseded. Neither ntab nor group-ntab is in build.sbt. All five proposed work stages remain open and need current frame4s API/consumer revalidation. Their support and lineage principles remain useful, but this epic must not pull effort from core correctness, measured performance, or active PHRF. Reactivate only for a concrete workflow that the current domain and estimate-set APIs cannot adequately serve; reduce scope before implementation.

Historical proposal:
Objective:
Build ntab as ScalaFIM's neuroimaging feature-relation layer on top of the ScalaFIM-incubated but domain-independent Frame foundation.

Explicit dependency:
This epic is blocked by the Frame foundation extraction/readiness gate. It does not depend on the optional Frame adapters epic, Gale, DuckDB, or Polars. The architecture plan may be rebased after the Frame type/API spike, but ntab implementation starts only against stable Frame schemas, expressions, plans, row selections, grouping, and local execution contracts.

Division of responsibility:
Frame owns general scalar relations: runtime and typed schemas, Arrow-compatible scalar columns, expressions, filtering, projection, grouping keys, inner/left joins, ordering, normalization, local reference interpretation, and generic source/sink semantics.
ntab owns neuroimaging features: stable feature references, exact volume/surface/parcel support, explicit resolution, feature codecs, support-aware reductions, contributor lineage, drill-down, and leaf domain bridges.
Large images and surface payloads are resolved domain values, not arbitrary Arrow cells. Frame may be named within ScalaFIM during incubation but has no ScalaFIM domain dependencies.

Canonical workflow:
inspect DynamicFrame -> bind a typed Frame schema -> filter/group metadata in Frame -> bind ntab feature handles -> validate exact support -> resolve selected payloads -> reduce/compare -> inspect receipt -> drill to contributors -> optionally prepare group inference through group-ntab.

Non-negotiable constraints:
- Dynamic schema discovery remains primary; typed evidence is bound at runtime boundaries.
- No implicit resampling, topology correspondence, parcel alignment, or missing-as-NaN policy.
- Metadata operations never trigger feature IO.
- dataset, group, mvpa, multivar, and lower modules do not depend back on ntab; integration bridges are leaves.
- ntab does not recreate Frame's column store, relational IR, normalization rules, reference interpreter, or generic IO capability system.

Epic acceptance:
All child gates close; JVM and Scala.js pass the defining workflow; group-ntab proves inferential integration; docs and build edges show the one-way dependency; and a future Frame extraction requires only a controlled dependency/package rename in ntab, not a change in scientific semantics or architecture.
